deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a derivation. It is part of the historical introduction to Riemann's Habilitationsschrift 'Über die Darstellbarkeit einer Function durch eine trigonometrischen Reihe' (written 1854, published posthumously by Dedekind in 1867). The page closes §1 and opens §2. Folio 9r supplies the context: the 18th-century vibrating-string controversy.

(a) End of §1. It continues a sentence from the previous page. D'Alembert accepted Euler's differential-calculus approach but challenged the correctness of Euler's results: for completely arbitrary functions one cannot know whether their derivatives are continuous.
- All three (Euler, d'Alembert, Lagrange) agreed that Daniel Bernoulli's trigonometric-series solution was not general.
- D'Alembert had to claim that even an analytically given periodic function cannot always be represented by a trigonometric series. He needed this to call Bernoulli's solution less general than his own (Opuscules I, p. 42, art. XXIV).
- Lagrange believed he could prove that such a representation is possible (Misc. Taur. III, p. 221, art. XXV).

(b) §2. Almost fifty years passed without essential progress. Then Fourier's remark opened a new epoch, which soon showed itself in major extensions of mathematical physics. Fourier observed that in the series
 f(x) = a_1 sin x + a_2 sin 2x + ... + (1/2) b_0 + b_1 cos x + b_2 cos 2x + ...
the coefficients are given by
 a_n = (1/π) ∫_{-π}^{π} f(x) sin(nx) dx,
 b_n = (1/π) ∫_{-π}^{π} f(x) cos(nx) dx.
Fourier saw that this way of determining the coefficients stays applicable even when f is completely arbitrary. The sentence breaks off at 'er setzte für f(x) eine so ge-[nannte ...]'.

Implicit step (mine): the coefficient formulas follow by multiplying the series by sin(nx) or cos(nx), integrating term by term over [-π, π], and using orthogonality. The factor 1/2 on b_0 makes the single formula for b_n also valid for n = 0.
errors: No mathematical errors. The coefficient formulas are correct and consistent with the (1/2) b_0 convention.
The term-by-term integration behind Fourier's formulas is not justified here. This is precisely the issue the rest of Riemann's essay addresses, so it is intentional, not a slip.

results.what: Euler–Fourier coefficient formulas for a trigonometric series, with the 1/2 b_0 normalization
results.usually_credited_to: Euler (c. 1777) and Clairaut earlier; systematized by Fourier (1807/1822)

results.what: Historical account of the vibrating-string controversy (Euler, d'Alembert, D. Bernoulli, Lagrange) and of Fourier's new epoch
results.modern_name: History of the vibrating string controversy
results.usually_credited_to: This account is well known as Riemann's own, from §§1–2 of his 1854 Habilitationsschrift (published 1867)

deep.surprise_reason: This is the draft or fair copy of the published historical introduction to Riemann's Habilitationsschrift. It is well known and contains only standard Fourier coefficient formulas. The only differences are small wording variants: here 'in der Behandlung willkürlicher Functionen', where the print reads 'in der Frage über die analytische Darstellbarkeit willkürlicher Functionen'.

checkable.asserts: Orthogonality of the sines, which underlies the coefficient formula for a_n
With the 1/2 b_0 convention, the constant term for f(x) = x^2 equals its mean, π^2/3

transcription_corrections: 'während d'Alembert¹) um Bernoulli's Lösung' should read 'während d'Alembert¹), um Bernoulli's Lösung' (comma; the 'um' begins the infinitive clause).
'als die seinige er-klären' should read 'als die seinige, erklären' (comma as in the printed text).

'Fast funfzig Jahre vergingen ohne dass in der Behandlung willkürlicher Functionen': the manuscript reading appears correct. It differs from the printed version ('fünfzig ... in der Frage über die analytische Darstellbarkeit willkürlicher Functionen').
Last line: 'eine so ge-' presumably continues as 'eine so genannte ...' on the next folio.
